**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The fix for issue 1836 is correct, complete, and proven value-neutral in the goldens. One process note: the PR is a draft, and its merge base is old. The merging session must do the quick pass, flag it ready, and take `git merge origin/main` at merge time (see the last section).

## What I read

- The PR diff: 167 files. No Rust source file changed. The change is in 5 `.cps` posts, 28 test files, 132 golden `.nc` files, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, and one decision entry.
- Issue 1836 (body and comments): a `P1` wrong-G-code defect. A Fanuc control with parameter 3401#0 DPI=0 reads `Z14` as 0.014 mm.
- The post code in `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `fanuc-lathe.cps`, and the new test `decimal_point_fanuc_family.rs`.
- `docs/decisions/1836-fanuc-decimal-point.md`.

## What I built and tested (local, worktree at the head, debug)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (full, 60 test binaries) | PASS - 0 failed |
| `decimal_point_fanuc_family` (3 pinning tests) | PASS |
| 16 touched `camcraft-app` test binaries (posting, lathe_post*, control_comp, probe_op, program_units, rotary_feed_cap, wear_comp, and the rest) | PASS, each binary green |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Trial merge with current `main` (`git merge-tree`) | clean, no conflicts |

## Golden audit (all 132 changed `.nc` files, machine-checked)

I checked every changed golden, not a sample. A script compared old and new line by line. Every changed line is the old line with a `.` inserted after a whole-number word. No digit, letter, value, or whitespace changed. No line was added or removed. Result: 4022 changed lines, all dot-only, in all 132 files. The goldens of the other posts (Sinumerik, Heidenhain, Tormach, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera, Sodick, Sinker) did not move. The probe macro lines (`IF[ABS[#5063-25]GT0.001]`, `#190=#100+17`) did not change. Manual spot checks across fanuc, haas, mazak, doosan-dnm, fanuc-lathe, inch and Explain goldens agree.

## What looks good

- The `pt`/`fn` split is right: address words carry the point, comment text and macro-B constants keep the trimmed form.
- The lathe `feedWord` guard moved from `w === "0"` to `Number(w) === 0`, so the refusal for a sub-increment feed still fires with the new form.
- The G76 `P`/`Q` and G83 `Q` words stay in whole least increments, as the control documents.
- The new pinning tests check all five posts, mm and inch, and scan for any bare length word in a motion block.
- The decision entry states the choice, the reason, the drops, and the kept words.
- No new crate dependency, no `Cargo.toml` change, no snapshot PNG, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. The file-size law holds: the touched `.rs` files grew only in files well under 400 lines.

## Notes and questions (not blocking)

1. `mazak.cps` line 798: `alarmUnless("ABS[...]LE" + fu(p.Tolerance))` still uses `fu` in a macro expression, where `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` moved the same line to `fn`. The output is the same for a tolerance that already has a point. It is a consistency gap only.
2. `fanuc-lathe.cps` line 907: the refusal text lost one space: `" - more than"` became `" -more than"`. No test pins this string. A one-character polish item.
3. The decision entry keeps whole-number feeds per minute without a point (`F300`) and argues the F word is not read in least increments. The #1836 fix targets the length words, and the Done-means line is met. It is worth one later check of the F-word behaviour in the parameter manual. A wrong feed does not move the tool to a wrong place, so this note does not change the verdict.

## Merge-time refresh is owed

The PR branches from `7c514c874` and `main` has moved on. GitHub reports MERGEABLE and my trial merge is clean. When this PR is next in a merge batch, take `git merge origin/main` on the branch first (class SAME if there are no hand edits), then merge. The draft state needs the quick pass and a `gh pr ready` before the merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
